title_as_printed: Experimental Results of Carbon Dioxide Solubility in Aqueous Solution of Sodium Chloride (1)-Sodium Sulfate (2)-Ammonium Chloride (3) Mixed Salt at 25 C and 1 atm
pressure_note: 'measured at 25 C and 1 atm partial pressure of carbon dioxide' (text, p. 190); title: 'at 25 C and 1 atm'; saturation method with correction for vapour pressure of the solution (estimated by the Robinson-Bower method from single-salt data)
volume_basis_evidence: 'Ostwald absorption coefficient, L, which is defined as the ratio of the volume of absorbed gas to the volume of absorbing liquid at the temperature and pressure of the measurement'; 'absorbing liquid' is the (gas-free) salt solution but the paper does not say solution vs solvent explicitly. Salt concentration Cs is 'total concentration of mixed salt (kmol m-3)' ('The molarity is used here as the salt concentration variable'), per volume of solution presumably, basis not spelled out.

composition.other_species: Total salt concentration Cs (kmol/m3 = mol/L) per row; salt shares are mole fractions in the salt mixture per block. Salts: NaCl, Na2SO4, NH4Cl (ternary mixed salt). NH4Cl is outside the six-ion set.

conversion_needs: Cs is a molarity (per volume of solution, presumably): conversion to molality needs solution density
Ostwald coefficient: converting to mole fraction needs CO2 molar volume and solution density
notes: Five (Table II) or three side-by-side blocks stacked left to right, one block label row each. The label row lists x1; x2; x3 (mole fractions of the three salts in the mixed salt). Blocks 1, 5 repeat Table I NaCl+Na2SO4 x1=0.50 and NaCl+NH4Cl x1=0.50 data (exact replicates kept).
